name: Health Policy
notes: Prerequisites of individual courses are not counted toward the major.
Students may major, minor, OR complete a cluster within the public health-related programs, but not more than one.
No more than two courses may overlap between a public health major and another major.
STAT 212 was valid until spring 2024; STAT 180 is the current course.
Several electives carry validity windows or class-year restrictions noted on the department page.
Electives must come from at least THREE different themes, and two must be from the Economics and Policy theme - the theme constraint is not auto-enforced.
NEEDS VERIFICATION: only the Economics and Policy theme was fully captured in the page snapshot; the remaining themes are modeled as related PHLT/PSCI/HIST/ECON courses.

requirementGroups.label: Public health general core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Public Health General Core (Four Courses): PHLT 101: Introduction to Public Health I; PHLT 103: Concepts of Epidemiology

requirementGroups.label: Statistics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: STAT 212: Applied Statistics I (valid until spring 2024) or STAT 180: Introduction to Applied Statistical Methodology (valid beginning fall 2024)

requirementGroups.label: Public health or medical ethics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: PHIL 228 (PHIL 228W): Public Health Ethics or PHIL 225: Ethical Decisions in Medicine

requirementGroups.label: Prerequisite: Principles of Economics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Pre-Requisite Courses (One Course): ECON 108: Principles of Economics

requirementGroups.label: Health policy core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Specific Core Requirements (Four Courses): ECON 207: Intermediate Microeconomics; PHLT 116: Introduction to the U.S. Health System; PHLT 230: Public Health Law & Policy

requirementGroups.label: US health policy history
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: HIST 373W (H): US Health Policy and Politics or HIST 374W (H): Pandemics, Politics, and Policies in the US
